h: וַיֵּלֶךְ וְשַׁבַּת תְּשׁוּבָה, כ׳ Vayeilech and Shabbos Shuvah, 20

p: Hashem is my shepherd; I shall not lack"
That is, when this becomes clear
that Hashem Yisbarach, who brings everything into being,
is the One who shepherds him,
then of itself he lacks nothing.
"though I walk, etc., I will not fear"
because it is clear before me
that even there "You are with me,"
that this too was from His providence, blessed be He.
For "Your rod and Your staff — they comfort me":
that through the rod of chastisement
is from His providence, blessed be He.
And this itself becomes a staff to comfort him,
"And you shall return unto Hashem your God"
there becomes known in his soul
שֶׁהַשֵּׁם הֲוָיָ"ה הוּא בַּעַל הַכּוֹחוֹת כּוּלָּם
that the Name Havayah is Master of all the forces,
and oversees and brings into being all the forces.
for it to become known in his soul
that the Name Havayah is "your God,"
And to this our Sages alluded
regarding the manna, which is called "white":
because it whitens the sins of Yisrael;
and Rashi of blessed memory explained
they would subjugate their hearts to the Omnipresent.
it is stated in the Gemara
thus they were found directing their hearts to the Omnipresent."
Here it is stated in the language of "directing."
"'And it came to pass, when Moshe raised his hand'
do the hands of Moshe, etc.?
Rather, when Yisrael would look upward
And likewise with the copper serpent:
And in truth the meaning is
as is stated in the Bartenura
regarding the juxtaposition of the mishnah,
which speaks above of the intention of the heart.
And why did it change to the language of "subjugating"?
of after the soul had already been touched
by the aspect of opposition and distance
from the serpent and from Amalek;
to subjugate one's heart to the Omnipresent
in which one had already become distant.
that it whitens the sins of Yisrael,
and Rashi explained in the language of "subjugating":
out of the state of distance,
through this their sins were whitened
they shall be white as snow"
